title: Vegetable Lo Mein with Mushrooms and Greens
changes_from_base: No meat, stock or oyster sauce; 200 g browned mushrooms, red pepper, carrot and greens with a soy sauce.
summary: This vegetarian version follows the classic lo mein method but leaves out meat, stock and oyster sauce, relying on browned mushrooms, red pepper, carrot and greens in a soy sauce for depth.
equipment: wok (35 cm) or large non-stick frying pan (30 cm)
small bowls for the prepared ingredients

ingredients.item: pak choi or choi sum, stems sliced, leaves halved
spring onions, cut into 4 cm lengths

steps.title: Cook the noodles
steps.text: This vegetable version follows the same soft-tossed noodle method as the chicken lo mein, with browned mushrooms standing in for meat and no oyster sauce, so it's vegetarian. Boil the noodles in 3 litres of unsalted water for 2-3 minutes until just tender, then drain and rinse briefly under warm water to remove surface starch. Shake dry and toss with the sesame oil.

steps.title: Mix the sauce
steps.text: Whisk together the light and dark soy sauces, sugar, water and cornflour in a small jug, ready to pour in later.

steps.title: Brown the mushrooms
steps.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in the wok over high heat and stir-fry the mushrooms for 3-4 minutes without crowding the pan, until they're browned and any liquid they've released has cooked away. Well-browned mushrooms bring a deep, savoury flavour that fills in for the meat in this version.

steps.title: Stir-fry pepper and carrot
steps.text: Add the remaining oil with the red pepper and carrot and stir-fry for 2 minutes until they soften slightly but keep some bite.

steps.title: Add aromatics and pak choi
steps.text: Stir in the garlic, ginger and pak choi stems for 1 minute, then add the leaves for a final 30 seconds, just long enough for them to wilt.

steps.title: Toss noodles in sauce
steps.text: Add the noodles and sauce to the wok and toss everything together for 1-2 minutes until glossy and evenly coated.

steps.title: Finish with spring onion
steps.text: Scatter over the spring onions, toss once more and serve straight away while hot.

tips: Don't crowd the mushrooms in the wok — if they're piled up, they'll release moisture and stew rather than browning properly.
Let the mushrooms' liquid cook off fully before moving on, as that browning is what gives this vegetarian version its savoury depth.
Add the pak choi leaves right at the end, since they wilt in seconds and go limp if added with the stems.
Cook the noodles until fully tender, as there's no second cooking stage to soften them further.
storage: Keep in a covered container in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat in a hot wok or microwave with a splash of water until piping hot throughout. This dish doesn't freeze well, as the pak choi and noodles turn soft and watery once thawed. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
